subject_identity_derivation.inputs: subject_kind K and a full 40-hex candidate commit SHA C.
steps: S1 C must name a COMMIT object (git cat-file -t C = commit); a tree or any other object fails. candidate_sha = C (40 lowercase hex). tree_sha = git rev-parse C^{tree}; tree_sha never equals candidate_sha.
S2 COVERED = every path of git ls-tree -r C that starts with any covered_path_prefix of K, sorted by byte order. COVERED must be non-empty.

S3 IMPORTED = the transitive closure, over files ending .ts .tsx .js .mjs in COVERED and then in IMPORTED, of every repository module they import: each import_specifier_grammar match whose specifier starts with "." (resolved against the importing file's directory) or "@/" (resolved against the repository root), resolved by trying the suffixes of import_resolution_suffixes in order against the tree of C; minus COVERED; sorted by byte order. A specifier of either form that resolves to no path fails the derivation. Package specifiers (neither "." nor "@/") are not followed.

S4 GOVERNING = every distinct match of the regular expression docs/ops/[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.json in the blob text of any COVERED or IMPORTED path at C, minus COVERED and IMPORTED, sorted by byte order. Every GOVERNING path must exist at C; a dangling reference fails the derivation.
S5 entries = COVERED entries, then IMPORTED entries, then GOVERNING entries, each {role, path, blob} in the order of its list, with blob = the git blob id of path at C.
S6 package_digest = lowercase hex sha256 over the UTF-8 concatenation, for each entry in order, of role + TAB + path + TAB + blob + LF.
S7 governing_families = distinct family(P) for P in GOVERNING, sorted, where family(P) = P up to and including the underscore before the first match of _v<digit>, or P itself if there is none.
S8 governing_family_members_at_candidate = [{path, blob}] for every path of git ls-tree -r C that starts with any governing family, sorted by path.
subject_identity_derivation.authority_pins: The GOVERNING entries ARE the exact authority pins governing the subject: the authority the subject and its imported modules cite, at the blob it had at the candidate.
subject_identity_derivation.failure: Any step that cannot be completed exactly fails the derivation; no occurrence may be written.

verdict.literal_rule: verdict_literal is the recertifier's exact verdict string, uppercase [A-Z0-9_]. Split on "_". Its class is the LONGEST verdict_class whose tokens form a proper suffix of the literal's tokens. The prefix (the tokens before that suffix) must be non-empty, its LAST token must be one of required_qualifier_tokens, EVERY prefix token must be in the CLOSED prefix_token_vocabulary or match version_token_pattern, and it must contain none of forbidden_prefix_tokens (a redundant denylist kept as a second barrier). Any other literal (a bare class, no class suffix, a negation, qualifier or unknown word anywhere in the prefix) is unparseable and STOPS; a recertifier literal outside the vocabulary is escalated, never re-spelled by the materializer. The vocabulary is extended only by a later independently certified Recovery amendment. The parsed class must equal verdict_class.
verdict.promotion_rule: Only a positive class with blocking_findings_count = 0 and an empty blocking_findings list becomes an occurrence. FAIL, BLOCKED and INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE are NEVER written as occurrences, under any literal, count or relabelling.
verdict.PASS_CLASS: In this contract and in every Recovery prerequisite that says "independently certified PASS", PASS-class means verdict_class PASS or PASS_WITH_NONBLOCKING_FINDINGS with zero blocking findings, every nonblocking finding recorded OPEN (see SECTION_D16 and OF-IS-8).

findings.rule: Every nonblocking finding the recertifier reported is recorded, each with status OPEN. nonblocking_findings has exactly nonblocking_findings_reported_count entries with unique non-empty string ids and non-empty summaries. PASS has zero; PASS_WITH_NONBLOCKING_FINDINGS has at least one.
findings.closure: A finding is closed ONLY by a later occurrence of the SAME kind whose chain.predecessor names the occurrence carrying it and whose closes_predecessor_findings lists its id. An occurrence never closes its own findings and never closes findings of an occurrence it does not name as predecessor.

roles.candidate_author: The lane that authored the candidate commit.
roles.independent_recertifier: The lane that independently recertified the candidate and issued the verdict. It records the candidate and tree it examined, the scope of its recertification and a reference to its report.
roles.materializer: The lane that writes the occurrence file.

provenance.independence: The three lane ids, compared after trim and uppercase, are non-empty strings and pairwise DISTINCT. A materializer that is the author, a recertifier that is the author, or a materializer that is the recertifier STOPS (STOP_PROVENANCE_NOT_INDEPENDENT). Git author identity is not a lane identity on this repository (every commit carries the same git author) and is never used for independence.

recert_scope.rule: independent_recertifier.scope is one of values and independent_recertifier.report_reference is a non-empty string naming where the report can be read (a PR comment URL, a lane transcript id, or a repository path). Anything else STOPS (STOP_RECERT_SCOPE_UNDECLARED). A consumer reads the scope; an occurrence never claims more than its recertifier examined.

evidence_basis.identity_facts_basis: MATERIALIZER_REDERIVED: the materializer re-derives SUBJECT_IDENTITY by subject_identity_derivation from git and records only values it derived.
evidence_basis.verdict_and_findings_basis: RECERTIFIER_REPORTED_SECOND_HAND: verdict, literal, scope, findings and counts are transcribed from the recertifier's report.
evidence_basis.materializer_reproduced_recert_evidence: Must be the boolean false. A materializer never claims to have reproduced the recertifier's tests, mutations, measurements or reasoning.

provenance.recert_subject_binding: independent_recertifier.examined_candidate_sha and examined_tree_sha must equal subject.candidate_sha and subject.tree_sha. A verdict about one commit cannot be recorded for another, including a different commit with the same tree.

path_and_identity.collision_resistance: Both are functions of (subject_kind, full 40-hex candidate_sha) only. Two different candidates can never share a path. A record whose path or package_id is not the derived one for its own subject_kind and candidate_sha STOPS.
path_and_identity.single_write: An occurrence path is written once. If the path already exists, the write STOPS (STOP_OCCURRENCE_PATH_EXISTS); an occurrence is never overwritten, amended or deleted. Any later change to its bytes makes it invalid at read time (STOP_OCCURRENCE_EDITED_AFTER_WRITE).

chain.rule: Occurrences of the same subject_kind form one chain. chain.predecessor is null for the first occurrence of a kind; otherwise it names {path, candidate_sha, package_digest} of the current chain TIP (the one occurrence of that kind no other occurrence names as predecessor). A predecessor that is not the tip, that is of another kind, or that has the same candidate_sha STOPS (STOP_CHAIN_PREDECESSOR_MISMATCH).
chain.serialization: Materializer lanes of the same subject_kind run one at a time. Each re-evaluates V11 against the target branch head immediately before its merge; a repository in which a kind has more than one tip is invalid for that kind (every occurrence of it is INVALID_AT_READ until a governed repair), and the companion test fails on it.
chain.no_silent_reuse: A later candidate never inherits an earlier occurrence: its own occurrence requires its own recertification of exactly that candidate (recert_subject_binding). A consumer may rely on an earlier occurrence at a later head ONLY through the currency rule below, citing that occurrence by path.

read_time_validation.rule: A CONSUMER at head H (an EA-F1 evaluation, an HX-2 evaluation, the #220 merge lane, the companion test) validates an occurrence found at H by: V1..V10 of validation_order, with V3 read as "the contract artifact at H has exactly the blob occurrence_contract.blob" (an in-place edit of this contract invalidates every occurrence written under it); plus R1: the occurrence path has never been deleted in the history of H and the file at H has exactly the blob it had in the FIRST commit that added it (STOP_OCCURRENCE_EDITED_AFTER_WRITE); plus R2: its kind has exactly one chain tip at H (STOP_CHAIN_PREDECESSOR_MISMATCH). V11 is WRITE-TIME only: at read time the occurrence's own path necessarily exists and an earlier occurrence is legitimately no longer the tip.
read_time_validation.derived_at_read: For a known subject (SECTION_D10) the derived identity is the recorded known-subject identity. For any other candidate it is re-derived from git at the candidate; a candidate that cannot be read is INVALID_AT_READ.

currency.rule: An occurrence is CURRENT at a consumer head H when all hold, in order: (1) it passes read_time_validation at H (else INVALID_AT_READ with the stop code); (2) COVERED at H by S2 is non-empty (else SUBJECT_NOT_PRESENT); (3) COVERED and IMPORTED at H by S2 and S3 equal the recorded COVERED and IMPORTED path lists (else STALE_COVERED_SET_CHANGED); (4) every COVERED and IMPORTED blob at H equals the recorded blob (else STALE_COVERED_PATH_CHANGED); (5) every GOVERNING blob at H equals the recorded blob (else STALE_GOVERNING_AUTHORITY_CHANGED); (6) every path at H under a recorded governing family is either a recorded governing_family_members_at_candidate entry with the same blob, or a declared_non_invalidating_governing_layers entry of that kind with the same blob (the contract artifact itself, whose integrity (1) establishes, is declared without a blob); a changed recorded member is STALE_GOVERNING_AUTHORITY_CHANGED and any other path is STALE_GOVERNING_LAYER_ADDED.
currency.not_invalidating: Any other commit -- a merge, a change to a path outside COVERED, IMPORTED, GOVERNING and the governing families -- does NOT invalidate an occurrence. Currency is decided by the subject's closure, not by commit identity of H.

Census execution evidence does not share those prefixes and does not invalidate.
explicit_invalidators_by_kind.OFFLINE_RECOVERY_IMPLEMENTATION_RECERT: A new or changed file under any covered prefix (including a new test under tests/recovery/), or a changed or newly imported repository module, is STALE by rules (3)/(4). declared_non_invalidating_governing_laye.rule: A governing layer added after a candidate does not invalidate that kind's occurrences only if listed here (or in a later independently certified Recovery amendment) with its blob and reason. V10 provenance independent (STOP_PROVENANCE_NOT_INDEPENDENT), recertifier examined exactly the subject (STOP_RECERT_SUBJECT_MISMATCH), scope and report reference declared (STOP_RECERT_SCOPE_UNDECLARED), no reproduction claim and the fixed bases (STOP_MATERIALIZER_REPRODUCTION_CLAIM).

V11 WRITE-TIME ONLY: path not already present (STOP_OCCURRENCE_PATH_EXISTS); chain predecessor is the current tip of the kind or null when none exists (STOP_CHAIN_PREDECESSOR_MISMATCH); closes_predecessor_findings valid (STOP_FINDING_CLOSURE_INVALID).
